To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of reputation- and context- and content- based trust mechanisms is a promising approach for the realization of flexible, task-specific trust policies for Semantic Web applications.

1) the usage of context information for trust decisions can be very helpful, 2) the combination of context- and reputation-based trust is a promising approach for a future Semantic Web Trust Architecture.

the Semantic Web can be extended by a flexible, fine-graned, and application-specific trust architecture that is based on reputation-, context- as well as content-based trust mechanisms, and that the usage of trust mechanisms based on application specific data can be a valuable addition to the current trust architectures on the Semantic Web.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of how to combine reputation-, context- (i.e. the context of an application) and content-based trust in a flexible and task-specific way to support the evaluation of the trustworthiness of Semantic Web resources.
a trust architecture that enables the definition and enforcement of fine-grained, context-sensitive trust policies on the Semantic Web.
the following research question: How to use the Semantic Web's potential to enable flexible and fine-grained trust policies on a Semantic Web?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a future trust architecture for the Semantic Web should not only focus on reputation-based trust but also on context- and contentbased trust mechanisms.
the Semantic Web will not be a single, homogeneous system, but rather a collection of different, heterogeneous sub-systems.

reputation- based trust mechanisms should be used as a basis for trust evaluations, but that they can and should be extended by context- and content- based trust mechanisms in order to allow for fine-grained and subjective trust evaluations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not only interested in the trust of a source in general, but also in the trust in a source for a specific purpose and with respect to specific data.
we propose a flexible trust architecture for the Semantic Web, which allows to use all available information to formulate task-specific trust policies.

we have developed and evaluated a trust architecture for the Semantic Web, which enables the formulation of trust policies that can combine different trust mechanisms and which is capable to handle the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of the Web.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Semantic Web can be extended by a trust architecture which supports a wide range of application-specific trust policies.
the usage of context and content-based trust can be a viable alternative or complement to reputation-based trust on the Semantic Web.
trust policies can be used for a flexible, fine-grined, and context- and content-aware trust management.
